$comment: One sentence per export that has no JSDoc in the source. A JSDoc description, once written, takes precedence.
AccessibilityAction: An action a screen reader offers on a view: a standard `name` or a custom one listed by `label`.
ActionSheetButton: One choice an action sheet offers, which may be the cancel choice, a destructive one or a dimmed one the user can't pick.
ActionSheetOptions: What an action sheet shows: the choices it offers the user, with an optional heading and, on iPad, where its popover points.
AlertButton: One button of an alert or a prompt, as the app lists it and as the call resolves with the one the user picked.
AlertButtonStyle: How an alert or action sheet button reads to the user: an ordinary choice, the one that cancels, or one that destroys something.
AlertOptions: What an alert says and which buttons it offers, and the base a prompt adds its text field to.
AndroidNeeds: Declares what a native module's Android side needs beside its Kotlin class: Gradle dependencies and the manifest entries it adds to the app.
AnimatableProps: The names of the props `animate` can move with a transition rather than set at once.
AppearancePreferences: The user's display preferences together, for tests and code that need both at once.
AudioPlayerOptions: Sets how an audio player starts out (its volume, speed and looping) and which scope owns it.
AudioRecorderOptions: Chooses the file an audio recorder writes, its quality, and whether it measures the input level while it records.
BackgroundTaskOptions: Tells the OS how often a background task may run and what the device must have (a network, a charger) before it does.
BarcodeEvent: Tells a Camera's app which code came into view, what it encodes and where it is in the preview.
Box: A plain container primitive laid out as a column, taking the container props and nothing more.
BoxProps: Props of `Box`: the container props (`ContainerProps`) and nothing more.
BundledImageSource: An image shipped inside the app, as importing a PNG or JPEG makes it, so an Image shows it with no request.
Button: A native button primitive showing text, with the text styling props and `disabled`.
ButtonProps: Props of `Button`: `TextProps` plus the native font and text props and `disabled`.
ByteRange: Picks the part of a file `fileSystem.readBytes` reads, for reading a header or a large file in pieces.
Calendar: One of the user's calendar settings, for showing dates, times and weeks the way the user reads them.
CameraFacing: Which camera a Camera uses: `'back'` or `'front'`.
CameraMethods: What an app can ask a mounted Camera to do through its ref: take pictures, record video and pause the preview.
CameraPicture: A picture a Camera took, as a JPEG file in the cache that an Image or `fileSystem` can use at once.
CameraProps: Props of `Camera`: `facing`, `flash`, `torch`, `zoom`, `mode`, `mute`, `barcodes`, and the `onReady`, `onError` and `onBarcode` handlers.
CameraReadyEvent: The Camera's `onReady` event, without payload: the preview runs and the camera can take pictures and record.
CameraRecording: A video a Camera recorded, as an MPEG-4 file in the cache with its length.
CaptureOptions: Tunes what the system camera captures for `mediaPicker.capture()`: images or videos, JPEG quality, a maximum size and the iOS editor.
ColorSchemeName: The platform's color scheme, `'light'` or `'dark'`, as `appearance.colorScheme` reports it.
CommonProps: The props every view accepts, for typing a component that passes them on to the view it renders.
Composable: Anything a view's `gestures` prop and the gesture composers accept: one gesture, or gestures already composed.
ComposedGesture: Several gestures on one view combined so they race, recognize together, or wait for one another to fail.
ContainerProps: The props every container view accepts, children included, for typing a component that wraps one.
ContentAlignment: CSS's content alignment keywords for `justifyContent` and `alignContent`, with their `safe` and `unsafe` overflow positions.
DecayConfig: Tunes how a `decay()` animation coasts to a stop from a velocity, and the range it stays within or rubber-bands past.
Divider: A separator line primitive, at least 1pt tall, taking only the common view props.
DividerProps: Props of `Divider`: the common view props and nothing more.
DownloadOptions: Adds request headers to a download and follows its progress.
DownloadResult: Where a finished download is on disk and what the server answered.
ElementHandle: A mounted view as code reaches it through a ref: to focus it, set a native prop directly, or listen for and dispatch events.
EventSubscription: A subscription to a native event, which `remove()` ends.
Extrapolate: How `interpolate` treats input outside its range: `'clamp'` to the ends, or `'extend'` linearly beyond them.
FillRule: Decides which parts of a self-intersecting shape a fill covers, as SVG's `fill-rule` does.
FlingDirection: Where a fling may go: `'left'`, `'right'`, `'up'` or `'down'`.
FlingEvent: Where a fling started, in the view and on screen, for reacting to the swipe that triggered it.
FlingOptions: Sets the directions a `fling()` gesture answers to, and the callbacks that run when it is recognized.
FocusEvent: A `KuitoEvent` of type `focus` or `blur`, as `TextField` passes to `onFocus` and `onBlur`.
FontWeight: A font's weight: `normal`, `bold`, or a number from `100` to `900` in hundreds.
ForProps: Props of `For`: the items in `each`, a `fallback` while empty, and a child that renders an item's row once.
Fragment: Groups children without adding a native view of its own.
FragmentProps: Props of `Fragment`: its `children` and the `key` every element accepts.
FunctionDeclarations: Declares, in a native module's spec, on which thread each of its functions runs.
GeocodedLocation: A position `location.geocode()` found for an address, ready to center a map or measure a distance.
HStack: A container that lays its children out horizontally.
HStackProps: Props of `HStack`: layout, decoration and gesture props of a horizontal container.
HitArea: Grows or shrinks the area that takes a gesture's touches beyond the view's bounds, so a small target stays easy to hit.
Image: Displays bundled or remote images with caching, placeholders and load/error events.
ImageErrorEvent: A `KuitoEvent` of type `error`, with the error payload, that `Image` passes to `onError`.
ImpactStyle: How heavy a collision `haptics.impact()` makes the device feel.
InterpolateOptions: Says what `interpolate()` does with input past its last stop: hold the end value, or keep going.
IosNeeds: Declares what a native module's iOS side needs beside its Swift class: Info.plist keys, frameworks and Swift packages.
KeyboardEventName: A keyboard event the runtime listens for: `willShow`, `didShow`, `willHide`, `didHide`, `willChangeFrame` or `didChangeFrame`.
KeyboardFrameEvent: What a keyboard event says about the keyboard's motion, for moving views in step with it.
KuitoCustomEvent: An event an app makes and dispatches through a view's element, with a payload of its own, for signalling between components without props.
KuitoElement: What a JSX expression evaluates to, before Kuito renders it.
KuitoNativeEvent: The event an element listener receives, with the DOM's methods to stop its propagation or cancel its default action.
LastKnownPositionOptions: Says how old and how coarse a cached fix `location.last()` may return before it resolves `null`.
LengthPercentageAuto: A length in points, a percentage of the containing block, or `auto`.
LinkProps: Props of `Link`: the `to` destination, whether to `replace` the current route, and `Pressable`'s props except `onPress`.
ListItem: What a List's `renderItem` receives for one row: the item, its position, and whether the row is on screen.
ListProps: Props of `List`: its `data`, `renderItem`, keys, sections, slots, layout and viewability options on top of `Scroll`'s.
LocationError: Why a location call or watch failed, for telling the user or falling back.
LocationHeading: Which way the device points, for a compass or for turning a map with the user.
LocationObject: One position fix of the device, with when it was taken and whether a mock location supplied it.
LocationOptions: Trades a fix's accuracy against the battery it costs.
LongPressEvent: Where a long press happened and how long it was held.
LongPressOptions: Sets how long a `longPress()` gesture must be held and how far the finger may wander, and its callbacks.
MatchProps: Props of `Match`: the `when` condition and the children, or callback, rendered while it is truthy.
MediaAsset: One image or video the user picked or captured, as a file in the app's cache with what it is.
MediaPickerResult: What the media picker ended with: the assets the user chose, or a cancel.
MediaType: What the media picker offers: `images` or `videos`.
NotificationType: A haptic notification's kind, `'success'`, `'warning'` or `'error'`, as `haptics.notification()` takes it.
PanChangeEvent: A pan's move, with how far the finger went since the last one.
PanEvent: Where a pan is, how far it has moved and how fast, as it starts and ends.
PanGesture: The gesture `pan()` makes, with `x` and `y` translation sources that motion values follow.
PanOptions: Restricts a `pan()` gesture to one axis or a distance before it starts, and sets its callbacks.
ParamValue: A route param's value: a `string`, `number` or `boolean`.
PermissionResponse: Whether the app holds a permission, and whether asking again can still show the system prompt.
PersistedOptions: Says where `persisted()` stores its value and the schema a stored value must still match.
PickOptions: Tunes the system photo picker for `mediaPicker.pick()`: what it offers, how many assets the user may choose, and their size.
PictureOptions: Tunes a picture a Camera takes: its JPEG quality, and whether its bytes come back with it.
PinchChangeEvent: A pinch's move, with how much the scale changed since the last one.
PinchEvent: How far a pinch has scaled and around which point, as it starts and ends.
PinchGesture: The gesture `pinch()` makes, with a `scale` source multiplying what the follower was when it activated.
PinchOptions: Sets a `pinch()` gesture's callbacks, and when and where it takes touches.
PrefetchOptions: Picks the caches `image.prefetch()` fills, so the Image that later shows the picture finds it there.
Presentation: How a route's screen appears: pushed onto its stack, or presented over everything as a sheet, a modal or full screen.
PressEvent: The `press` event a `Pressable`'s `onPress` receives: it bubbles, can be cancelled, and may carry the touch location.
Pressable: A container that takes presses: `onPress`, `onPressStart`, `onPressEnd` and `onLongPress` on top of a container's props.
Primitive: A built-in element: at runtime the string the renderer dispatches on, typed as a function so TSX checks its props `P`.
PromptOptions: What a prompt asks for: an alert's title, message and buttons, plus the kind of text field and its starting text.
PromptType: What a prompt asks the user to type: plain text, a password, or a login's username and password.
QueryOptions: Selects the rows a database query returns: which ones match, their order, and how many.
QueuedDeclaration: Declares a native module function that runs on the main thread or the module's background thread, returning a value or settling through a callback.
Recording: A finished audio recording, as a file the app can play, upload or keep.
RecordingOptions: Caps how long a Camera's video recording may run before it stops on its own.
RecordingQuality: Trades an audio recording's fidelity against its file size.
RemoteImageSource: An image an Image fetches by URL, with the request headers it needs.
RepeatConfig: Sets how many times `repeat()` plays an animation and whether every other run goes backwards.
Resource: Data a component loads when it mounts, read through signals, and loaded again on `refresh()`.
RotateGesture: The gesture `rotate()` makes, with a `rotation` source in degrees added to where the follower was.
RotateOptions: Sets a `rotate()` gesture's callbacks, and when and where it takes touches.
RotationChangeEvent: A rotation's move, with how many degrees it turned since the last one.
RotationEvent: How far a two-finger rotation has turned and around which point, as it starts and ends.
RouteProps: Props of `Route`: its `name`, `path`, `params`, `screen`, and how the screen is presented, titled and decorated.
RouterProps: Props of `Router`: the `initial` destination, whether deep `linking` is on, and the routes as `children`.
SafeArea: A `VStack` padded by the parts of the screen the system covers (status bar, notch, home indicator) on the `edges` given.
SafeAreaEdge: One screen edge `SafeArea` can pad: `top`, `right`, `bottom` or `left`.
Scalar: A plain value, a string, number, boolean or null; the kind `Animatable` props carry.
Scroll: A view that scrolls its content vertically or, with `horizontal`, sideways, with scroll, reach-end and pull-to-refresh events.
ScrollToIndexOptions: Says which item a List scrolls to and where in the viewport the item lands.
SecureStoreOptions: Chooses where a secret lives, when it can be read, and whether biometrics guard it.
SelfAlignment: Cross-axis alignment keywords for `alignSelf` and `alignItems`, each also with a `safe` or `unsafe` prefix.
ShapePaint: How a shape inside a Drawing is filled, stroked and moved, as SVG's presentation attributes; a Group passes its own to its shapes.
ShareAction: Whether the user shared from the share sheet or dismissed it.
ShareContent: What the share sheet shares: a message, a URL, or both.
ShareOptions: Platform touches for the share sheet: Android's chooser title, and iOS's subject and the activities it leaves out.
ShareResult: How the share sheet ended, and with which app or activity when the user shared.
Sheet: A native bottom sheet presenting its children above the screen, shown with `open` and resting at `snapPoints`.
ShowProps: Props of `Show`: the `when` condition, a `fallback` node, and children or a callback receiving the truthy value.
SliderEvent: The value a Slider settled on when the user let go, for saving it once rather than on every move.
SliderProps: Props of `Slider`: `value`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `disabled`, track colors, and the `onChange` and `onChangeEnd` callbacks.
Spacer: An empty view that grows (`flex-grow: 1`) to take the free space along its parent.
SpacerProps: Props of `Spacer`: the common props only, with nothing of its own.
Spinner: The native activity indicator, spinning while `animating` is true.
SpinnerProps: Props of `Spinner`: the common props plus `animating`.
SplashScreenProps: Props of `SplashScreen`: `Box` props plus the `logo` and `brand` part props, `onReady` and live `children`.
SpringConfig: Tunes how a `spring()` animation moves: by its physics, or by a duration and how bouncy it is.
StandardAccessibilityAction: The accessibility action names screen readers know: `activate`, `increment`, `decrement`, `longpress`, `magicTap` and `escape`.
StatusBarTransition: How the iOS status bar animates as it hides or shows.
StrokeLinecap: How the ends of an open stroke inside a Drawing look, as SVG's `stroke-linecap`.
StrokeLinejoin: How the corners of a stroke inside a Drawing look, as SVG's `stroke-linejoin`.
SubmitEvent: The text a TextField held when the user pressed its return key.
SwitchProps: Props of `Switch`: a `fallback` node and `Match` elements as children.
SymbolProps: Props of `Symbol`: the common props plus `name`, `size`, `weight` and `tintColor`.
SystemBarsProps: Props of `SystemBars`: the root `backgroundColor`, Android's navigation bar color, button style and hiding, `immersive` and the iOS home indicator.
Tab: One tab of `Tabs`: a stack of its own, shown in the native tab bar with its `title` and `icon`.
TabIcon: A tab's icon: a symbol name, `{ ios, android }` names per platform, or `{ uri }` for any image.
TabProps: Props of `Tab`: its `name`, `title`, `icon` and the routes it holds as `children`.
TapEvent: Where a tap landed, in the view and on screen.
TapOptions: Sets how many taps in a row a `tap()` gesture needs and how quick and still they must be, and its callbacks.
Task: An async operation an app starts on demand, whose progress, result and error components read as signals.
TaskContext: What a task's or resource's work receives first: the signal that aborts it when it is cancelled or replaced.
TaskOptions: Says what a task does when it is run again while a run is in flight: replace it, or reuse it.
Text: A text view: its `children` are the text it shows, styled by the font and alignment props of `TextProps`.
TextChangeEvent: A `change` event carrying `text`, a `TextField`'s text as the user changed it.
TextField: A native text input: `value` is two-way through a signal, with `placeholder`, `onChange`, `onSubmit`, `onFocus` and `onBlur`.
TextFieldProps: Props of `TextField`: every view's common props, the input's native props, and the `onChange`, `onSubmit`, `onFocus` and `onBlur` handlers.
TextProps: Props of `Text`: every view's common props, the native font and text props, and `children` as its text content.
TextSelection: A range of a TextField's text, for reading or setting the caret and what the user selected.
TimingConfig: Tunes a `timing()` animation's duration, easing and delay.
Toggle: A native on/off control: `checked` is two-way through a signal, and `onChange` reports whether it is on.
ToggleProps: Props of `Toggle`: every view's common props, `checked` and `disabled`, and `onChange` with whether it is on.
TouchesGesture: A `touches()` gesture, a pan from the first touch, whose `x` and `y` are where the finger is in the view.
TouchesOptions: Sets a `touches()` gesture's callbacks, and when and where it takes touches.
Truthy: `T` without its falsy members (`null`, `undefined`, `false`, `0`, `0n`, `''`): what a `Show` or `Match` branch callback receives.
UploadOptions: Says how a file is uploaded: the HTTP method and headers, as the whole body or a form field, and its progress.
UploadResult: What the server answered to an upload.
VStack: A container laying its children out vertically, taking the layout, decoration and gesture props of every view.
VStackProps: Props of `VStack`: the container props, `children` beside every view's common and native props, and nothing more.
ValueChangeEvent: A `change` event carrying a boolean `value`, as a `Toggle` reports being switched on or off.
VideoBufferEvent: A `Video`'s `buffer` event, with `isBuffering` saying whether the player is waiting for data.
VideoEndEvent: A `Video`'s `end` event, sent when playback reaches the end; it carries no payload.
VideoErrorEvent: A `Video`'s `error` event, with the failure's `code` and `message`.
VideoFullscreenEvent: A `Video`'s `fullscreenChange` event, with `fullscreen` saying whether the player is now full screen.
VideoHandle: What a Video's ref holds, for seeking, playing, pausing and entering full screen or picture in picture from code.
VideoLoadEvent: A `Video`'s `load` event, with the `duration` (null for a live stream), `currentTime` and `naturalSize` in pixels.
VideoPictureInPictureEvent: A `Video`'s `pictureInPictureChange` event, with `active` saying whether picture in picture is on.
VideoPlaybackStateEvent: A `Video`'s `playbackStateChange` event: `isPlaying`, the `currentTime` in seconds and the playback `rate`.
VideoProgressEvent: A `Video`'s `progress` event, sent while playing: `currentTime` and the buffered `playableDuration`, in seconds.
VideoProps: Props of `Video`: `src`, `paused`, `muted`, `volume`, `rate`, `loop`, `objectFit`, `controls`, its events, and every view's common props.
Viewability: Says how much of a List's row must be on screen before its `visible` signal turns true.
WatchPositionOptions: Trades how often and how precisely a position watch reports against the battery it costs.
WebViewNavigationEvent: A `WebView`'s `loadStart`, `load`, `loadEnd` or `navigate` event, carrying the page's `url`, `title`, `loading` and history state.
WebViewProps: Props of `WebView`: `src` or `html` to load, `allowedOrigins`, `injectedJavaScript`, `userAgent`, and its load, navigation, error and message events.
WindowOrientation: Whether the window is taller than wide or wider than tall, for picking a layout.
WindowSize: The window's size, for layouts that depend on the space the app has.
WriteOptions: Says whether `fileSystem.write()` replaces the file or adds to its end.
accessibility: Adapts the app to assistive technology: whether a screen reader runs or the user prefers reduced motion, and speaking or moving focus for them.
app: The app's place in the system: whether it is in the foreground, memory warnings, and opening its settings.
appearance: Follows the user's light or dark mode and preferred text size.
appearance.AppearancePreferences: The user's display preferences together, for tests and code that need both at once.
appearance.ColorSchemeName: The user's color scheme, `'light'` or `'dark'`, as `appearance.colorScheme` reports it.
audio: Plays and records audio, and configures how the app's sound mixes with other apps' and reacts to interruptions.
audio.AudioPlayerOptions: Sets how an audio player starts out (its volume, speed and looping) and which scope owns it.
audio.AudioRecorderOptions: Chooses the file an audio recorder writes, its quality, and whether it measures the input level while it records.
audio.Recording: A finished audio recording, as a file the app can play, upload or keep.
audio.RecordingQuality: Trades an audio recording's fidelity against its file size.
backgroundTasks: Runs the app's JavaScript periodically while it is in the background, when the OS allows it.
backgroundTasks.BackgroundTaskOptions: Tells the OS how often a background task may run and what the device must have (a network, a charger) before it does.
brightness: Brightens or dims the screen while the app needs it, such as for a code to scan, and gives control back to the system.
cameraRef: Makes a `CameraRef` while a component sets up: a Camera ref whose `ready` and `error` signals follow the view's events.
clipboard: Copies text to the system clipboard and pastes from it.
clipboard.writeText: Puts `text` on the clipboard, replacing its content.
config.AndroidIntentFilter: One `android.manifest` intent filter, checked: the links and intents that open the app, and whether its hosts are verified as app links.
config.ColorScheme: The `colorScheme` setting: whether the app follows the system's light or dark mode or stays in one.
config.IOSBackgroundMode: One value of `ios.backgroundModes`: a `UIBackgroundModes` entry such as `audio`, `location` or `fetch`.
config.IOS_BACKGROUND_MODES: The `UIBackgroundModes` values `ios.backgroundModes` accepts, from `audio` and `location` to `push-to-talk`.
config.KuitoFontWeight: A bundled font's weight: `normal`, `bold`, or a hundred from `100` to `900`.
config.KuitoSplash: The `splash` setting: how the native launch screen looks, in light and dark mode, and the named variants the app can pick for its next launch.
config.Orientation: The `orientation` setting: `default` follows the device, `portrait` or `landscape` locks the app.
config.PlistDictionary: A property-list object with string keys and `PlistValue` values, as `ios.infoPlist` and `ios.entitlements` take.
config.PlistValue: A property-list value: a string, number, boolean, an array of values, or a `PlistDictionary`.
config.PushEnvironment: The `ios.pushEnvironment` setting: the APNs server a build's remote push uses, `development` for builds Xcode signs for development and `production` for TestFlight and the App Store.
config.SoftInputMode: The `android.softInputMode` setting: what the window does for the keyboard, `resize` or `pan`.
config.SplashConfig: The `splash` setting checked, with defaults applied: one `SplashLook` and each variant as its own `SplashLook`.
config.StatusBarStyle: The status bar's content color at launch: `light`, `dark`, or `auto` to follow the color scheme.
db: Stores the app's structured data in SQLite tables whose queries and counts components read as signals.
db.QueryOptions: Selects the rows a database query returns: which ones match, their order, and how many.
device: Fixed facts about the device the app runs on, read from the platform once on first use.
device.manufacturer: The device's manufacturer, `Apple` on iOS and `Build.MANUFACTURER` on Android, read once on first use.
device.osBuildId: The operating system's build identifier, or null when the platform does not report one.
device.osVersion: The version of the operating system the app runs on.
device.type: What kind of device the app runs on: `'phone'`, `'tablet'`, `'desktop'`, `'tv'` or `'unknown'`.
fileSystem: Reads and writes files in the app's sandbox, and downloads and uploads them with progress.
fileSystem.ByteRange: Picks the part of a file `fileSystem.readBytes` reads, for reading a header or a large file in pieces.
fileSystem.DownloadOptions: Adds request headers to a download and follows its progress.
fileSystem.DownloadResult: Where a finished download is on disk and what the server answered.
fileSystem.UploadOptions: Says how a file is uploaded: the HTTP method and headers, as the whole body or a form field, and its progress.
fileSystem.UploadResult: What the server answered to an upload.
fileSystem.WriteOptions: Says whether `fileSystem.write()` replaces the file or adds to its end.
fileSystem.exists: Whether anything, a file or a directory, is at a `file://` URI.
fileSystem.info: What is at a `file://` URI, if anything: whether it is a directory, its size and when it last changed.
fileSystem.read: Reads a whole file as UTF-8 text, rejecting with `ERR_ENCODING` when it isn't text.
fileSystem.write: Writes text as UTF-8, or an ArrayBuffer's bytes as they are, to a file, replacing it or adding to its end.
fonts: Loads font files at run time, for families the app does not bundle through `kuito.config.ts`.
fonts.FontWeight: A font file's weight: `'normal'` (400), `'bold'` (700), or 100 to 900 in hundreds.
global.AbortController: Makes a signal and cancels whatever it was given to, a `fetch` or a task, with an optional reason.
global.AbortSignal: Cancels a `fetch` or other work it is given to; `AbortSignal.timeout()` makes one that fires after a delay.
global.BodyInit: What a `fetch` request body may be: a string, `ArrayBuffer`, `ArrayBufferView` or `URLSearchParams`.
global.HeadersInit: What `Headers` and `RequestInit.headers` take: a `Headers`, name-value pairs, or a record of strings.
global.RequestInit: Shapes a `fetch` request: its method, headers and body, and a signal that cancels it.
global.Response: A `fetch` response, for checking its status and reading its body whole or as it streams in.
global.TextEncoder: Turns strings into UTF-8 bytes, for hashing, uploading or writing them.
global.URLSearchParams: The `URLSearchParams` constructor Kuito's runtime provides, taking a query string, pairs, a record or another instance.
global.WebSocket: A WebSocket connection, for messages a server pushes to the app as they happen.
global.clearInterval: Cancels an id from `setInterval` or `setTimeout`, which share ids; undefined is ignored.
global.clearTimeout: Cancels an id from `setTimeout` or `setInterval`, which share ids; undefined is ignored.
global.crypto: The platform's CSPRNG, with `getRandomValues` and `randomUUID`; no SubtleCrypto.
global.queueMicrotask: Runs `callback` in the microtask queue, before the next task.
global.setTimeout: Runs `callback` with `args` after `delay` milliseconds and returns an id `clearTimeout` cancels.
haptics: Plays haptic feedback, so a selection, a collision or an outcome can be felt as well as seen.
haptics.ImpactStyle: The weight of the collision `haptics.impact` plays: `'light'`, `'medium'` or `'heavy'`.
haptics.NotificationType: The outcome a `notification` haptic reports: `'success'`, `'warning'` or `'error'`.
image: Works with the images an Image shows, ahead of showing them.
image.PrefetchOptions: Picks the caches `image.prefetch()` fills, so the Image that later shows the picture finds it there.
keyboard: Follows the software keyboard, for layouts and animations that react to it, and dismisses it.
keyboard.KeyboardFrameEvent: What a keyboard event says about the keyboard's motion, for moving views in step with it.
linking: Opens URLs in other apps, and reads the link that opened this one.
localization: Follows the user's languages, region, calendar and clock, for formatting text, numbers and dates their way.
localization.Calendar: One of the user's calendar settings, for showing dates, times and weeks the way the user reads them.
location: Finds where the device is and which way it points, and turns addresses into positions.
location.GeocodedLocation: A position `location.geocode()` found for an address, ready to center a map or measure a distance.
location.LastKnownPositionOptions: Says how old and how coarse a cached fix `location.last()` may return before it resolves `null`.
location.LocationError: Why a location call or watch failed, for telling the user or falling back.
location.LocationHeading: Which way the device points, for a compass or for turning a map with the user.
location.LocationObject: One position fix of the device, with when it was taken and whether a mock location supplied it.
location.LocationOptions: Trades a fix's accuracy against the battery it costs.
location.WatchPositionOptions: Trades how often and how precisely a position watch reports against the battery it costs.
mediaPicker: Lets the user pick photos and videos from their library, or take new ones with the system camera.
mediaPicker.CaptureOptions: Tunes what the system camera captures for `mediaPicker.capture()`: images or videos, JPEG quality, a maximum size and the iOS editor.
mediaPicker.MediaAsset: One image or video the user picked or captured, as a file in the app's cache with what it is.
mediaPicker.MediaPickerResult: What the media picker ended with: the assets the user chose, or a cancel.
mediaPicker.MediaType: What the picker offers, `'images'` or `'videos'`, named by the `mediaTypes` option.
mediaPicker.PickOptions: Tunes the system photo picker for `mediaPicker.pick()`: what it offers, how many assets the user may choose, and their size.
network: Follows whether the device is online and what kind of network it is on, for deferring work on an expensive or missing connection.
network.CellularGeneration: The radio's generation on a cellular network: `'2g'`, `'3g'`, `'4g'` or `'5g'`.
network.NetworkDetails: Whether the current network costs the user money, and its generation on cellular.
network.NetworkState: The device's network as the app can use it now: its kind, whether it is connected, and whether the internet answers.
notifications: Shows local notifications, now or at a time, and registers for remote push.
onCleanup: Registers `fn` to run when the component's instance is disposed, without running it on mount.
permissions: Checks and requests the runtime permissions device features need, with one status model across them.
permissions.PermissionResponse: Whether the app holds a permission, and whether asking again can still show the system prompt.
ref: Makes a stable `ElementRef` to a native view while a component sets up; `current` holds the handle.
resource: Loads data for a component once it has mounted, with its progress, result and error as signals and `refresh()` to load it again.
secureStore: Keeps small secrets, such as tokens, in the platform's encrypted storage.
secureStore.SecureStoreOptions: Chooses where a secret lives, when it can be read, and whether biometrics guard it.
secureStore.delete: Deletes the secret under `key`, found by key and `keychainService` alone.
splash: Controls the native launch screen: keep it up while the app loads, hide it, or pick the look of the next launch.
storage: Keeps small strings across launches by key, like a `Map` that survives restarts.
storage.SqlStatement: One SQL statement and the values bound to its placeholders, for running raw SQL.
storage.clear: Removes every key `storage` holds, on the module's background thread.
storage.delete: Removes the value under `key`, on the module's background thread.
storage.deleteMany: Removes the values under `keys` in one transaction, on the module's background thread.
storage.getMany: The values under `keys`, as `[key, value | null]` entries in `keys`' order.
storage.keys: Every key `storage` holds, in no particular order.
storage.set: Stores the string `value` under `key`, replacing what was there.
task: Makes a `Task` running `work` on demand with an abort signal, under a `replace` or `drop` policy.
tests.CostCounter: The name of one cost counter, for reading or budgeting a single measure of an interaction's work.
tests.Edges: Insets on each edge of the test's screen, in points, such as what the status bar and home indicator cover.
tests.FontTable: The fonts a test measures text with, so its layouts come out the same on every machine or match a device's.
tests.ModuleFakes: Fakes for the native modules a test's app calls, by module name, so the app runs without a device.
tests.PressOptions: Makes `press` hold past the long-press delay, to test `onLongPress`.
tests.Queries: Finds views as a user finds them, by their text or their role and accessible name.
tests.Rect: A view's frame in points, for asserting where layout put it.
tests.ReplayOptions: Describes the device a recording came from, its fonts and its window, so a replay lays out as it did.
tests.Replayed: The tree a replay left beside the one the device recorded, for comparing them in a golden test.
tests.RoleOptions: Narrows a role query to the view with this accessible name.
tests.ScrollOffset: Where `scroll` moves a Scroll or a list to, in points along each axis.
tests.TextMatch: The text a query looks for: an exact string, or a pattern.
tests.assert: Node's strict assertions, typed for a Kuito test file, for checking what the app shows and did.
tests.describe: Groups related tests under one name, as Node's test runner does.
tests.replay: Replays a recording a device saved on the headless host, for a golden test that the layout still matches the device's.
tests.test: Declares one test, as Node's test runner does, run by `kuito test` on the headless host.
videoRef: Creates a `VideoRef` while a component sets up: a `Video` ref with playback state signals and `time`/`duration` motion values.
webViewRef: Creates a `WebViewRef` while a component sets up: a `WebView` ref with `url`, `title`, `loading` and history signals.
window: Follows the app's window: its size, the insets the system covers, its orientation and its width class.
window.WindowOrientation: Whether the window is taller than wide or wider than tall, for picking a layout.
window.WindowSize: The window's size, for layouts that depend on the space the app has.
